costGuide.title: Jaguar AJ6 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a Jaguar AJ6 engine typically takes 12-16 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent) due to the age of the host vehicles and the need to carefully manage aging ancillary components, cooling hoses, and wiring looms .
paragraphs: The final Jaguar AJ6 engine cost depends heavily on the condition of the cylinder head and whether the head gasket has already failed. Opting for a reconditioned unit that includes a renewed multi-layer steel (MLS) head gasket, updated oil cooler seals, and a refreshed timing chain assembly provides the best long-term value. For a detailed breakdown of what influences these figures across different conditions, see our full reconditioned engine cost guide.

failures.title: Jaguar AJ6 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Head Gasket Failure - 3.6L and 4.0L variants
items.whatHappens: The AJ6’s all-aluminium block and cylinder head are susceptible to head gasket degradation, often exacerbated by aging cooling systems, perished hoses, or a failed viscous cooling fan clutch. Symptoms include unexplained coolant loss, white exhaust smoke, and mayonnaise-like oil contamination. If ignored, localized overheating can lead to warped cylinder heads or catastrophic engine seizure.
items.repairVsReplace: While a head gasket replacement is mechanically possible, the labour-intensive nature of the job on an older Jaguar, combined with the risk of hidden warpage, often makes a full reconditioned engine replacement more cost-effective and reliable.

items.title: Oil Cooler Seal Leaks
items.whatHappens: The oil cooler, mounted on the side of the block, uses rubber seals that harden and perish over time. This results in external oil leaks dripping onto the subframe or, in worse cases, internal failure allowing oil to mix with the coolant.
items.repairVsReplace: Seal replacement is a straightforward and inexpensive fix if caught early. However, if coolant contamination has already occurred and circulated through the galleries, a full engine strip and clean or a reconditioned replacement is required to prevent bearing failure.

items.title: Timing Chain Stretch and Guide Wear
items.whatHappens: Although more robust than later Jaguar engines, high-mileage AJ6 units can experience timing chain stretch and plastic guide wear. This leads to a distinct rattling noise on cold starts and potential cam timing inaccuracies, affecting engine performance.
items.repairVsReplace: A timing chain kit replacement is a viable repair, but it is frequently bundled into a full reconditioned build to ensure maximum longevity and quiet operation for the classic chassis.

failures.goodYearsLine: The later 4.0L iterations of the AJ6 (often badged as the AJ16 in its final production years) featured revised cylinder heads, improved gasket materials, and updated engine management, making them notably more resistant to head gasket failure than the early 3.6L units .

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement AJ6 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used Jaguar AJ6 engine for sale can be a viable, budget-friendly option for lower-value XJ40 or XJS projects, provided the seller can supply documented evidence of a recent head gasket replacement and timing chain service. Without this verifiable history, the risk of inheriting an overheating-related failure is significant. Learn more about used engines.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: For most classic Jaguar owners, a reconditioned AJ6 is the optimal choice. A proper recon will proactively address the engine’s known weaknesses by fitting an updated multi-layer steel (MLS) head gasket, new oil cooler seals, and a refreshed timing chain assembly, delivering near-new reliability for the future. Explore reconditioned engine options.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for concours-restoration XJS or XJ40 projects where the engine is being stripped to the bare block. This allows for line-boring the main bearings, fitting oversized pistons if the bores are scored, and comprehensive balancing, ensuring the engine matches the pristine condition of the restored chassis. View rebuilt engine services.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting your replacement through our vetted network ensures the work is completed by specialists familiar with classic Jaguar wiring and ancillary systems, backed by a nationwide warranty. Check supply and fit availability.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Classic Jaguar XJ40 and XJS models typically hold values between £4,000 and £15,000, depending on condition, mileage, and provenance. Because a full reconditioned AJ6 replacement can represent a significant portion of a lower-value example's worth, it is crucial to evaluate the vehicle's overall condition and scrap or part-exchange value before committing to a major mechanical investment. If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value before committing.

items.question: How much does a Jaguar AJ6 engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Jaguar AJ6 engine typically costs between £2,500 and £4,500 for supply only, with fitted prices ranging from £3,150 to £5,500 depending on the specialist. Used units start around £800 but carry a higher risk of inherited cooling issues. Full rebuilt units can exceed £6,000 for concours-level restoration specifications. Compare AJ6 engine prices from vetted UK specialists.

items.question: What is the most common failure on the Jaguar AJ6 engine?
items.answer: The most documented failure on the AJ6 is head gasket degradation, often exacerbated by aging cooling systems, perished hoses, or a failed viscous fan clutch. Oil cooler seal leaks are also highly prevalent, leading to external drips or internal coolant contamination. High-mileage units may experience timing chain stretch and plastic guide wear. Compare rebuilt AJ6 prices with these common failures already addressed.

items.question: Which Jaguar models use the AJ6 engine?
items.answer: The AJ6 engine was fitted exclusively to the Jaguar XJ (XJ40 generation) and the Jaguar XJS between 1986 and 1997. It was offered in 3.2L, 3.6L, and 4.0L displacements. The 4.0L version was later revised and rebranded as the AJ16 in the final years of production. Check compatibility for your specific XJ40 or XJS model.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned AJ6 engine?
items.answer: For a classic Jaguar, a reconditioned AJ6 is almost always the better long-term investment compared to a used unit. Used engines often inherit the same aging head gasket and oil cooler seal issues that caused the original failure. A proper reconditioned build replaces these weak points with updated materials, such as multi-layer steel (MLS) gaskets. View our guide on choosing between used and reconditioned engines.

items.question: How do I know if my car has the AJ6 engine?
items.answer: You can confirm your engine code by checking the V5C registration document under the "Engine Number" field or by locating the code stamped on the front of the cylinder block. The AJ6 is an inline-six petrol engine, easily distinguished from the later V8 (AJ-V8) or V6 (AJ-V6) configurations. Confusing it with the successor AJ16 is common, but the AJ16 features a different cylinder head and engine management system. Enter your registration above to confirm your exact fitment.
